entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen30311" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen30312" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen30313" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen30313" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen30312" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen30314" type="x-p"/> God commands Jeremiah to write down in one roll or volume all the predictions he had uttered against Israel and Judah, and all the surrounding nations, from the day of his vocation to the prophetic office, that the house of Judah might have abundant warning of the dreadful calamities with which their country was about to be visited, if not prevented by a timely repentance, <reference osisRef="Jer.36.1-Jer.36.3">Jer 36:1-3</reference>. The prophet employs Baruch the scribe, the son of Neriah, to write from his mouth all the words of the Lord, and then to read them publicly upon a fast day in the Lord's house, <reference osisRef="Jer.36.4-Jer.36.8">Jer 36:4-8</reference>. A general fast is proclaimed in the following year, viz., the fifth year of the reign of Jehoiakim; upon which occasion Baruch, in obedience to the prophet's command, reads the words of Jeremiah to all the people at the entry of the new gate of the temple, <reference osisRef="Jer.36.9">Jer 36:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.36.10">Jer 36:10</reference>. The princes, hearing of this, send for Baruch, who reads the roll to them; at the contents of which they are greatly alarmed, and solemnly resolve to give information to the king, at the same time advising both the prophet and his scribe to hide themselves, <reference osisRef="Jer.36.11-Jer.36.19">Jer 36:11-19</reference>. Jehoiakim likewise having sent for the roll, Jehudi reads to him a part; and then the king, though advised to the contrary by some of has princes, having cut the leaves, throws the whole into the fire, <reference osisRef="Jer.36.20-Jer.36.25">Jer 36:20-25</reference>, and orders Jeremiah and Baruch to be seized; but they could not be found, because a special providence of God had concealed them, <reference osisRef="Jer.36.26">Jer 36:26</reference>. Jeremiah is commanded to re-write his prophecies, and to denounce the judgments of God against the king who had destroyed the first roll, <reference osisRef="Jer.36.27-Jer.36.31">Jer 36:27-31</reference>. Baruch accordingly writes from the mouth of Jeremiah a new copy, with numerous additions, <reference osisRef="Jer.36.32">Jer 36:32</reference>. <div eID="gen30314" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30315" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen30315" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30316" type="x-p"/> And it came to pass in the fourth year - About the end of this year, see <reference osisRef="Jer.36.9">Jer 36:9</reference>. This discourse also bears its own date, and was probably delivered at a time when the people enjoyed peace, and were about to celebrate one of their annual fasts.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen30316" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30317" type="x-p"/> Take thee a roll of a book - Take a sufficient quantity of parchment; cut and stitch it together, that it may make a roll on which to write the words that I have already spoken, that they may serve for a testimony to future generations. The Jewish rolls, several of which now lie before me, were made of vellum, or of sheep-skins dressed in the half-tanned or Basil manner. These were cut into certain lengths, and those parts were all stitched together, and rolled upon a roller. The matter was written on these skins in columns or pages. Sometimes two rollers are used, that as the matter is read from the roll in the left hand, the reader may coil it on the roller in his right. In this form the Pentateuch is written which is read in the synagogues.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen30321" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30322" type="x-p"/> Then Jeremiah called Baruch - This man, so useful to the prophet, and so faithfully attached to him, was by office a scribe; which signifies, not only a writer, but also a man in office; a chancellor, secretary, etc., a learned man; one acquainted with laws and customs.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 22</hi> <div eID="gen30328" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30329" type="x-p"/> Winterhouse - A warm apartment suited to the season of the year, (December), when in Palestine there is often snow upon the ground, though it does not last long. A fire on the hearth - a pan or brazier of burning coals. This is the case to the present day. In cold weather the rich burn wood in brass or earthen pans, placed in any part of the room; the indigent burn sticks on the floor.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 30</hi> <div eID="gen30335" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30336" type="x-p"/> He shall have none to sit upon the throne of David - He shall have no successor and himself shall have an untimely end, and shall not even be buried, but his body be exposed to the open air, both night and day. He who wishes to hide his crimes, or take away the evidence which is against him, adds thereby to his iniquities, and is sure in consequence to double his punishment. See the threatening against Jehoiakim, <reference osisRef="Jer.22.19">Jer 22:19</reference> (note), and the note there.
